THE BLACK ENVELOPE

Before anyone explains how the Academy works, the intake printer gives one mechanical cough.
Then it prints nothing.
Instead, a black envelope slides from the tray.
No stamp.
No sender.
One strange mark: 0.
Inside is a blank Detective Academy Recruit Credential.
No name.
No call sign.
No detective assigned.
A mistake?
A coincidence?
OR AN INVITATION MEANT FOR YOU?
WILL YOU CLAIM IT?

ORIENTATION
BEFORE YOU DECIDE

The Detective Academy is where small real-world mysteries become case files.
New calls, reopened records, and strange pieces of evidence arrive through the Academy intake desk.
Take a look inside.
This is how it all begins.

WHAT TO EXPECT
01 CLUE INSPECTION
02 READING WITNESS STATEMENTS
03 COMPARING EVIDENCE
04 STUDYING MAPS & COORDINATES
05 DECODING MESSAGES
06 FOLLOWING PATTERNS
LOOK CLOSER. CHECK THE FACTS. LET THE EVIDENCE LEAD.
WHAT YOU ARE ABOUT TO WALK INTO
The Academy is not one room, and this investigation will not happen in one afternoon.

30 CONNECTED CASE FILES
Witness-board mysteries, map and coordinate puzzles, visual evidence, secret codes, timelines, sequencing challenges and logic deductions.

A TEAM THAT THINKS TOGETHER
The Happy Makers will be your team.
They compare clues, trade theories, drop case notes, make jokes at extremely professional moments and point out things worth checking.

YOU MAKE THE CALL
They do not get to make your verdict for you.
The cases get harder as your investigation grows.

STRANGER THINGS HAPPEN
A trophy returns before anyone logs it. A box marked EVIDENCE lands where it should not. Later, solved maps and forgotten records begin to matter again.

WHAT IS ROOM ZERO?
And somewhere inside the Academy, one question keeps returning:
LET'S MEET THE HAPPY MAKERS

MEET THE HAPPY MAKERS
THE ACADEMY FIELD TEAM

WHO THEY ARE
Six detectives.
Six different ways of looking at the same mess.
They compare clues, challenge each other's theories and keep asking questions until the story starts to make sense.

HOW THEY WORK
Clues first.
Theories second.
Arguments occasionally.
Then they test what actually fits and quietly retire the theory that sounded brilliant five minutes ago.

WHY A TEAM?
Because no one notices everything.
Luckily, they rarely miss the same thing.
Bad news for mysteries.

THE SQUAD
MEET THE HAPPY MAKERS // FIELD TEAM 01

MIMI
FIELD DETECTIVE // CASE CAPTAIN
Runs the case table.
Finds the tiny clue.
May need help finding her own phone.
STRENGTH: Turns a muddle into the next useful step.
FUNNY HABIT: Organizes everything except what she just put down.
SMALL CLUES. BIG IDEAS.

LULI
FIELD DETECTIVE // CLUE ANALYST
Reads the small print.
Questions the big claim.
Spots contradictions.
Short replies. Long books.
STRENGTH: Spots contradictions and tests what evidence proves.
FUNNY HABIT: Can forget a book is not a substitute for lunch.
SMALL QUESTIONS. BIG DISCOVERIES.

DILO
FIELD DETECTIVE // CODE & TECH
Loves codes, games and close scores.
Connects numbers, machines and clever experiments.
Will help you test them.
STRENGTH: Finds patterns and connects the dots.
FUNNY HABIT: His confidence can finish before the test does.
TEST THE IDEA. TRY THE EXPERIMENT.

MIMI: I've got a plan! ...actually, wait, where's my phone?
LULI: Facts first. Opinions later. Snacks somewhere in between.
DILO: If it's weird enough to beep... it's probably important.

THE SQUAD
MEET THE HAPPY MAKERS // FIELD TEAM 01

NINI
FIELD DETECTIVE // PEOPLE & COURAGE
Gives nervous people room to speak.
Notices feelings and details everyone skipped.
Asks small, surprisingly good questions.
STRENGTH: Looks beyond the obvious.
FUNNY HABIT: Can become fond of a theory before it earns its place.

ALIO
FIELD DETECTIVE // ROUTES & RECON
Asks the extra question.
Checks the unexpected corner.
Packed a helmet for this introduction.
STRENGTH: Notices routes and useful physical details.
FUNNY HABIT: Prepares for imaginary dangers before reading ordinary signs.

GRANDMA BIBI
ARCHIVE MENTOR // OLD ACADEMY GUIDE
Knows old shelves and stranger stories.
Connects historical records and knows what to verify.
Says when a memory is incomplete.
Stops nonsense without putting down her team.
STRENGTH: Finds context and the missing pieces.
FUNNY HABIT: Remembers the adventure; the date may need a label.

NEXT: CLAIM YOUR RECRUIT CREDENTIAL
The Academy can invite you. Only you can choose to step in.
CLAIM YOUR RECRUIT CREDENTIAL

If you are in, this is the moment.
No one else can fill this out for you.

DETECTIVE ACADEMY // RECRUIT CREDENTIAL
DETECTIVE NAME:
OFFICIAL CALL SIGN:
MY BEST DETECTIVE SKILL:
SIGNATURE:
FIRST CASE DATE:
ACADEMY STATUS: RECRUIT

Your best detective skill can be anything useful: noticing tiny details, remembering odd facts, asking good questions, staying calm, drawing maps, spotting patterns - or something only you know how to do.
The credential gets you into the investigation.
The cases decide what kind of detective you become.

HOW EVERY CASE WORKS
YOU NEVER NEED TO GUESS WHAT TO DO NEXT. EVERY CASE FOLLOWS THE SAME SIMPLE RHYTHM.

1 CASE FILE - WHAT HAPPENED?
Read the story first. It tells you where the case came from, what happened, and why this deduction matters.
2 YOUR OBJECTIVE
One exact thing to prove, find, sort, decode or reconstruct.
3 EVIDENCE
Witness boards, maps, photographs, records, codes, timelines, scraps and strange Academy files.
4 HAPPY MAKERS CHAT
The squad thinks out loud, jokes, questions theories and helps you notice what deserves attention.
5 MAKE THE CALL
Use the response made for that case: circle it, mark it, sort it, enter the code or write the coordinate. Then move on.
6 SAVE IT?
Only some cases send something to the Case Wall. When the book says “CASE WALL → PAGE 13”, copy that item there. Otherwise keep the verdict on the case page.

MAP CASES
READ THIS ONCE

Some cases use an Academy floor grid to reconstruct where people were standing.
Read these rules once. Later map cases will only give you the case-specific key.
1 HOW TO READ A COORDINATE
Letters run across the columns.
Numbers run down the rows.
D3 = column D, row 3.
Use one coordinate system: the labels printed beside the grid you are solving.
2 STANDARD MAP CASE RULES
1. Place every witness exactly once.
2. Each witness finishes in a different row and a different column.
3. Use only printed witness statements and visible map features.
4. If a case asks for a room or area companion, that person is a lead for the next interview, not automatically guilty.
5. Keep every final witness position on the completed map. Do not erase it after writing the verdict.
3 MAP LEGEND
PERSON MAY STAND ON: open numbered/coordinate squares shown as usable floor space.
SQUARE BLOCKED BY: walls, fixed furniture, equipment or other clearly illustrated obstacles.
ROOM / ZONE: named areas on the map. If a rule specifically says ROOM, a ZONE does not count.
There is no secret gray category. If something is blocked, the map shows why.

NEXT UP: YOUR CASE WALL + HINT VAULT
THE NEXT PAGE IS YOUR CASE WALL. HERE'S HOW IT WORKS:

1 FIND THE PAGE
CASE WALL → PAGE 13
Go to the next page to see your Case Wall.
2 COPY THE ITEM
When the book tells you to, copy the correct item to the matching spot on the wall.
3 SOLVE WITH CLUES
Use the items on your Case Wall to spot connections and answer the big questions later.

DILO: So we just copy stuff to the wall? Easy!
LULI: Yes! But the right stuff. Wrong clues = confused detectives.
ALIO: The Case Wall helps us see the big picture. Clues make more sense together!
NINI: It's like a puzzle! The messier it looks at first, the more fun it is to solve.
BIBI: Details matter! One small clue can change everything.
MIMI: A detective without key notes in one place is like solving a case with 37 tabs open and 2% battery. Bold, chaotic, doomed.

HINT VAULT + SOLUTION FILES
Stuck? Use the Hint Vault at the back of the book.
HINT LEVEL 1: A small nudge.
HINT LEVEL 2: Narrow the search.
HINT LEVEL 3: A bigger push.
SOLUTION FILES: Full answers at the back.

CASE WALL // RECORD ZONES
Copy here only the items the book explicitly tells you to keep. Write clearly. Keep it tidy.
MATCHING MARKS
MESSAGES / RULES
CODES / COORDINATES
OPEN QUESTIONS
Not every case sends something here. Save only what the book tells you to save.

30 ACTIVE FILES
REAL MYSTERIES. BRIGHT MINDS. YOUR TURN.

No answers here. Just doors.
Turn the page. Case 01 is waiting.

SOMETHING IS OFF
THE FILES ARE REAL.
THE TEAM IS READY.
BUT SOMETHING DOESN'T FIT.
IT'S TIME TO LOOK CLOSER.

THE ENVELOPE THAT WAS NEVER DELIVERED
CASE 01 // TRAINING // MISSION ACTIVE

Your Recruit Credential is barely signed when Mimi slides the black-envelope file back across the Case Table.
The printer log gives you one solid fact: the envelope was released from internal Academy stock.
No courier. No outside delivery.
Four visiting helpers were in the intake area at that exact minute.
The strange 0 can wait.
First, you need the cleanest thing the record can still prove:
WHO WAS STANDING AT DELIVERY WHEN THE ENVELOPE EMERGED?
TRAINING NOTE: This first grid teaches the Academy map method. Later map cases use the same logic with fewer obvious starting points.

MIMI: Internal stock. Good. We start with what we can prove.
ALIO: Or we investigate my leading theory: a secret tunnel and a mini van delivery. Very efficient. Very suspicious.
LULI: A tunnel, a minivan, and zero evidence. Impressive start, Alio.
NINI: Let's park the minivan for a minute and follow the facts first.
DILO: Agreed. If the tunnel appears later, I'll happily upgrade the theory.
CASE 01 // THE INTAKE GRID

YOUR OBJECTIVE
IDENTIFY who was at Delivery when the black envelope emerged and record their square.
INVESTIGATION RULES
Place each helper once on the 4x4 intake map.
Each helper uses a different row and a different column.
Combine row clues, column clues and relative clues before using elimination.
HELPER ROSTER // QUILL / PIP / MORSE / KNOX

WITNESS BOARD
WITNESS STATEMENTS
01 QUILL was in row 1.
02 PIP was in row 3.
03 MORSE was in column C.
04 KNOX was in column D.
05 PIP was somewhere to the left of QUILL.
06 MORSE was in a lower row than KNOX.
